title: Check
description: One rule the engine applies: a check whose query reports each problem it finds.

title: Product setting
description: A product's settings: the most children of one kind a record of the product should hold, the most entities an aggregate should hold, and the words that name technology in its essential records.

title: Page
description: One place in the app, identified by its address, showing a view of one loaded workspace.

title: Space
description: One product as a place to work in, in the rail.

title: Nav entry
description: An entry of the nav that folds, and whether the reader has it folded.

title: Tab set
description: The tabs open in one space, in order, with one active.

title: Tab
description: One place among the tabs: its focus and stage, its view, and its own history of where the Reader went in it.

title: Session settings
description: How the graph is laid out and how wide the wiki card is, for this browser session.

title: History entry
description: One place a tab went to, in its own Back and Forward history.

title: View
description: A place in an interface a person uses. It has no owner: it exists because it presents commands and queries, a person sending or asking each there, so a step that invokes one is carried out in it in an app a person works in. Its product follows from its ID, and it belongs to the one domain whose commands and queries it presents, or is shared when it presents two or more domains', or none.

title: Endpoint
description: An endpoint that exposes exactly one command or query, its parent. Flow steps reach it through their command or query, never directly.

title: Integration
description: An outside system the product exchanges with, such as a payment provider or a mail service. It has no owner: it exists because flow steps exchange with it, its product follows from its ID, and it belongs to the one domain whose flow steps exchange with it, or is shared when two or more do, or none.

title: View requirement
description: One rule a view must follow, such as what it shows while loading or a field's limits; built by the UI components whose code does what it says.

title: API requirement
description: One rule an endpoint must follow, such as an error's response or a limit on its request.

title: UI component
description: A piece of the user interface that renders one or more views and builds the view requirements its code does. It has no owner: it exists because views use it, its product follows from its ID, and it belongs to the one domain that uses the views it renders, or is shared when two or more do, or none.

title: Endpoint handler
description: Serves its endpoint: reads the request, calls the command or query handler and writes the response.

title: Adapter
description: Talks to its integration's outside system, so the rest of the code does not.

title: View test
description: Proves its view requirement in the view.

title: Endpoint test
description: Proves its API requirement at the endpoint: the request and the response.

title: Integration test
description: Proves an exchange with its integration's outside system.

title: Domain
description: A part of the product with its own model, language and owner, for one business capability: what DDD calls a bounded context. Domains meet only through published events.

title: Capability
description: An ordered slice of a domain that groups its use cases, such as Catalog or Lending.

title: Aggregate
description: The consistency boundary: a cluster of entities changed together as one unit, by one command at a time. Other aggregates follow its changes through events, and refer to it by ID only.

title: Entity field
description: One field of an entity, in order.

title: Entity
description: A record the domain keeps, with an identity: its aggregate's root or one of its children. Its fields are its entity fields, in order; the value objects it has are the ones its fields are typed with.

title: Invariant
description: A rule that holds for one aggregate on every change, enforced by its rule in the aggregate's code. Uniqueness across records (no two members share an email) is an invariant too, which a unique key of the table may back up.

title: Domain event
description: An unchangeable record that something happened to an aggregate, named in the past tense (Loan opened), raised by its commands. What it carries are its event fields.

title: Storage requirement
description: What the business needs kept of one aggregate or read model, and how well: its statement. It is built by its aggregate's repository or read model's reader once that names its data store, and proved by its storage requirement tests.

title: Storage requirement test
description: Proves its storage requirement at the level that can observe it: a round trip, a restart, a failed save that leaves nothing behind, a deletion, a restore.

title: Term
description: A word of the domain's glossary and what it means there, so specs, code and conversation use one language.

title: Value object
description: A value with no identity of its own, such as an email address or a money amount, defined by its fields and checked by its constraints when it is created. It has no owner: it exists because entities, events or read models use it as a field's type, its product follows from its ID, and it belongs to the one domain whose fields it types, or is shared when two or more domains use it, or none.

title: Value object field
description: One field of a value object, in order. A table stores a value object's fields flattened among its entity's own.

title: Constraint
description: A value object's own rule, checked when the value is created, such as an email address having one @.

title: Specification
description: A named predicate over one or more aggregates of one domain (Evans), such as Member in good standing. Commands check it before acting, and queries may select by it. It has no owner: it reads its aggregates, and its domain follows from its ID.

title: Event field
description: One field a domain event carries, in order. A published event's fields are a contract with other domains.

title: Command
description: A request to change exactly one aggregate: the one its entity belongs to. It sits under the entity it changes, and checks specifications, raises events and may call domain services, all of its own domain.

title: Read model
description: A view of its domain's data shaped for reading, which reads one or more of the domain's aggregates. Its fields are its read model fields, and it is stored in a table of its own.

title: Read model field
description: One field of a read model, in order. Its table's stored fields follow from it.

title: Query
description: A question asked of one read model, its parent. It changes nothing, and may select by specifications and call domain services of its own domain.

title: Policy
description: Whenever an event, then a command (event storming). It belongs to the command it invokes and hears one event: its own domain's, or another domain's published one. As it acts it may exchange with integrations of its product, as a flow step does.

title: Domain service
description: Domain logic that belongs to no single entity and is not a yes-or-no check, such as calculating a late fee. Commands and queries of its domain call it; it uses no storage and no outside system.

title: Repository
description: Loads and saves its aggregate, whole: the way command handlers reach the aggregate's storage. It persists exactly one aggregate, linked with persists, and sits under its domain, or, for one several domains share, under the domain that holds what they share.

title: Data model
description: Its entity in code: the entity's data, behavior and mapping to its table. A command is carried out by its handler and its aggregate root's data model.

title: Value type
description: Its value object in code, which checks the value object's constraints when a value is created.

title: Predicate
description: Its specification in code: a yes-or-no test over the records it is given.

title: Event type
description: Its domain event's shape in code; a contract with other domains when the event is published.

title: Projection
description: Fills its read model's table and keeps it current, from events or as a view's query. It writes only its own read model's table.

title: Command handler
description: Carries out its command: an application service that owns the transaction, loads the aggregate through its repository, checks specifications and raises events. What clean architecture calls a use case or interactor.

title: Query handler
description: Answers its query from its read model's table: an application service that changes nothing.

title: Event handler
description: Carries out its policy: hears the policy's event and sends its command.

title: Service
description: Its domain service in code. It never uses a repository or an outside system: its inputs are passed in, and it returns a value or a decision.

title: Constraint test
description: Proves its constraint: the values its value object accepts and refuses.

title: Invariant test
description: Proves its invariant: a change that would break it is refused, and the aggregate stays as it was.

title: Specification test
description: Proves its specification: which records satisfy the predicate and which do not.

title: Policy test
description: Proves its policy: when its event happens, its command is sent.

title: Domain service test
description: Proves its domain service: from the inputs given, the value or decision it returns.

title: Reader
description: Reads its read model's table for the read model's query handlers: the one way they reach its storage. It reads only its own read model's table, which the projection alone fills.

title: Rule
description: Its invariant in code: the rule in the aggregate's rules.ts that the aggregate's commands run before saving and every load runs over all data, named as its refusal names it. An invariant is built only through its rule.

title: Panel
description: One part of the view's layout, which always shows the view's focus and can be hidden without losing it.

title: Theme
description: One theme: a named set of token values with a light set and a dark set.

title: Product window
description: One window showing one product folder.

title: Recent folder
description: One folder the person opened lately, for File › Open Recent and the next launch.

title: App server
description: What one window loads Lathe from.

title: Appearance
description: The person's appearance: the theme in use, the color mode and Scroll to zoom.

title: Recent folders
description: The list of recent folders, one per shell.

title: Product repo
description: A product repo: its root folder, the schema version its data is for, where its data files are, and the other products it shows as a workspace.

title: Shell settings
description: The editor the shell opens data files in, its custom command, and where `claude` is.

title: Key bindings
description: The person's key bindings: the shortcuts they changed, in the order first changed.

title: Shortcut binding
description: One shortcut whose keys the person changed: its keys now, or none when they left it without a key on purpose.

title: Voice settings
description: The person's voice settings: the two modes and the phrases the voice grammar reads.

title: Window chat
description: One product window's chat, kept by the window's folder.

title: Product
description: A product: the root of its specifications and its own space, whose records link only to each other, with the roles its use cases and interfaces name, the kinds and relations it declares, and its open questions.

title: Product kind
description: A kind a product adds to Lathe's, such as a report or a terminal command. Its records sit under one parent kind, and its fields are its product kind fields.

title: Role
description: A role the product's records name, such as Owner, Reader or Agent: a use case's actors and a question's owner. Specs name roles, never people.

title: Interface actor
description: One role that uses an interface, in order: a role of the interface's product. A step's actor through the interface is the first of its use case's actors the interface lists.

title: Journey
description: A summary-level goal reached through several use cases, of one or more actors, in order: what starts it in the world (its trigger), what it ends in (its result), its steps and its journey test, and the business outcomes it serves (serves).

title: Journey step
description: One step of a journey, in order on its path, in the journey's words. It carries out one use case of the journey's product, of any domain, or one of its policies as a handoff, or nothing yet: a use case still to write. Who acts is its use case's actors; a handoff's actor is the product itself.

title: Journey test
description: The journey's acceptance test: its main path end to end, from its trigger to its result, across its use cases and handoffs, at the lowest level that can observe the result. It proves the journey only, never its steps' use cases.

title: Open question
description: Something undecided, with the role that decides it. It sits under its product or one of its domains, and may be about any record (the about link). A decided question is removed and its answer written into the records it affects.

title: Product kind field
description: One typed field of a product kind, in order.

title: Product relation
description: A pair of kinds a product lets a relation link. A new relation name gets its own link table; a name Lathe already has adds the pair to that relation, when its link table's ends accept the two kinds.

title: Interface
description: A way the product is used, such as an app a person works in, calls other programs make, or a command line: the root of its own aggregate. It offers use cases of its product, is used by some of the product's roles and follows the pattern that says how a step is carried out through it, so its version of each flow it offers is derived, never written.

title: Business outcome
description: A measurable change the product exists to bring about: its statement, measure and target, and what measures it (measured_by).

title: Extension record
description: A record of a product's own kind: an ID, a title, its one parent and the fields its kind declares, with the links it starts and the packages it uses.

title: Data store
description: Where data actually lives, named as in code or config, with its kind.

title: Table
description: Where an entity or a read model, its parent, is stored, in a data store or not; or, under a domain, a table of the domain's own infrastructure that implements no design record, such as its outbox. Its stored fields follow from its parent's fields, a value object's fields flattened among them, so it stores only what fields cannot say: its keys and indexes (its table keys). An entity's table holds its records, the source of truth: a table, normalized, or the browser storage, file or memory that keeps them; a read model's is a projection that can be rebuilt, usually a view over its domain's entity tables, or computed in memory on each load.

title: Table key
description: One key or index of a table, in order: its primary key, a unique key with the invariant it enforces, a foreign key with the table it points at, or an index. A foreign key points at a table of the same domain: a reference to another domain's aggregate stays a plain ID.

title: Standard
description: A library of rules that holds across the product: a quality, what its people need whatever it is built with (essential), or engineering, how its code is built (accidental). What follows one of its rules meets it.

title: Standard rule
description: One rule of a standard. Technical records that follow it link to it with meets; its standard rule tests prove it.

title: Standard rule test
description: Proves its standard rule in the product's code, such as a scan of the code for what the rule forbids: any number per rule, at any level.

title: Entry point
description: A start-up file: what runs first and wires the rest together, under the domain it starts.

title: Tooling
description: A dev script or config file outside the running product, under the domain whose code it builds, checks or tests.

title: Pattern following
description: A domain or use case that follows one pattern.

title: Setting value
description: A setting value: the value a following use case, or a domain that follows the pattern itself, gives one of the pattern's settings.

title: Slot filling
description: A technical record that fills one slot (a `fills` link).

title: Provision
description: A technical record or obligation and what provides it (a provided-by link).

title: Test data set
description: What some tests start from: the environment, the accounts and the starting records, how to prepare and reset them, and the file that builds them. Tests link to it with starts_from.

title: Use case
description: An actor's goal: its actors, its UC requirements and its one flow, the same through every interface that offers it. It changes nothing itself; its flow's steps invoke commands and queries.

title: Slot
description: An open-ended part of a pattern that code fills against its contract; a hand-written record that fills it is a fill.

title: UC requirement
description: One rule a use case must follow. Steps of the use case's own flow fulfill it.

title: Pattern
description: Behavior several use cases share, stated once: its settings (the known ways it varies), its rules and its slots (the open-ended parts code fills).

title: Pattern rule
description: One rule of a pattern. Every domain that follows the pattern owes it, with no exception.

title: Pattern setting
description: One setting of a pattern, in order: what each follower decides.

title: Flow
description: How its use case is carried out, whatever the interface: the steps on its main path and its alternate paths. A use case has one flow, and each interface that offers the use case has its own version of it, derived from the steps' commands and queries by the interface's pattern.

title: Flow step
description: One step of a flow, in order on its path, in the words of the people who take it. It fulfills UC requirements of its own use case, invokes at most one command or query and may exchange with integrations; where it is carried out is its interface's, derived. A step only one interface can do is a variant of that interface.

title: Use case actor
description: One actor of a use case, in order: a role of the use case's product.

title: Use case test
description: Proves its UC requirement, at the level the use case is stated: what the actor does and what the product does in answer.

title: Flow test
description: The use case's acceptance test: its flow's main path, end to end, through any one interface that offers the use case, at the level that fits that interface. How each other interface carries a step out is proved once per rule and domain by its pattern's rule tests.

title: Pattern rule test
description: Proves its pattern rule in one domain that adopts the pattern: one test per pattern rule and adopting domain.
